{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVIgqiM8AAAABXCzieA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm76XzhAmUfs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm76X", "number": 5, "title": "Implement an end-to-end Qwen 4B LoRA fine-tuning and evaluation workflow", "body": "## Problem

The repository can install and diagnose an Apple Silicon MLX environment (Issue #3), but it cannot yet run a local LLM, benchmark its code-generation ability, fine-tune it with LoRA, or compare performance before and after training. These four capabilities are needed to measure whether fine-tuning actually improves the model.

## Expected outcome

Provide a small, reproducible end-to-end experiment on a 4B-class Qwen model using MLX/MLX-LM on Apple Silicon:

1. Generate responses with a downloaded model.
2. Evaluate **baseline** Python code-generation performance on held-out MBPP problems.
3. Fine-tune with **LoRA** on disjoint training examples and save an adapter locally.
4. Re-evaluate the adapted model on the **same held-out examples** and report the difference in test-pass rate.

The README should let a developer run each stage separately and reproduce the comparison. Keep model weights, datasets, adapters, and experiment outputs out of Git.

## Context

- Repository: `takahirox/llm-finetuning`, default branch `main`. Issue #3 / PR #4 established Python 3.12, `uv`, MLX, MLX-LM, an environment checker, and ignore rules.
- Target hardware: Apple Silicon MacBook Pro with a Max-series chip; exact unified memory is not a required assumption.
- Aim: a **learning-effect experiment** using Python code generation, not a production service.
- Use an actual, publicly available **4B-class Qwen model** supported by the chosen MLX-LM version. During implementation, verify and document the exact model identifier/revision, license/usage terms, and any conversion needed instead of assuming an unverified model ID.
- Use a clearly separated MBPP training split and held-out evaluation split. Do not put evaluation prompts, reference solutions, or test cases into the fine-tuning examples.
- Follow the existing English-language, Issue → PR → review → merge policies in [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md).

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Model inference
- [ ] Provide a documented command to load the selected 4B-class model and generate a Python solution for a user-supplied task. Support base-model inference and inference with a locally saved LoRA adapter.
- [ ] Make model selection, decoding settings, and adapter path explicit and reproducible. Store/download weights outside version control and give helpful errors for missing model files or unsupported environments.

### Dataset and baseline evaluation
- [ ] Provide a reproducible data-preparation path for MBPP, with **non-overlapping** training and held-out evaluation sets, documented split/version and any fixed sample-selection seed.
- [ ] Provide an evaluation command that records a per-problem generated solution and a deterministic success/failure result based on MBPP test assertions, plus an aggregate **pass@1/test-pass percentage**.
- [ ] Evaluate the base model without any fine-tuned adapter and persist a machine-readable baseline result. Avoid evaluation-data leakage into the training set.
- [ ] Treat model-generated code as untrusted. Document the risks and implement a bounded, explicit evaluation-execution strategy (for example isolation, time limits and resource controls); do not silently run unbounded arbitrary code on the host.

### LoRA training
- [ ] Provide a runnable Apple Silicon MLX-LM LoRA workflow that uses only the training split; document essential parameters (model, seed, learning rate, steps/epochs, batch size, LoRA settings) and the invocation.
- [ ] Save adapters/checkpoints and training metadata to ignored local paths, not Git. Preserve the base weights, and support resuming/reusing a saved adapter for inference/evaluation where supported.
- [ ] Keep the first workflow minimal: no full fine-tuning, QLoRA-vs-LoRA sweep, hyperparameter search, web UI, or CI pipeline.

### Before/after comparison and reproducibility
- [ ] Evaluate base and LoRA-adapted models using **identical held-out examples, prompt construction, decoding/test settings, and scoring logic**.
- [ ] Provide a command or script that reads the two evaluation result files and reports baseline score, fine-tuned score, absolute percentage-point difference, and per-problem outcome changes. It must not imply that improvement is guaranteed.
- [ ] Persist useful experiment provenance (model/revision, dataset/split, configuration/seed, adapter reference, library versions, timestamps where relevant) so results can be interpreted and rerun.
- [ ] Extend README with copy-and-run commands for inference, data preparation, baseline evaluation, LoRA training, adapted evaluation, and comparison, including expected local output paths and practical memory/time caveats. Preserve existing setup and contributor links.

### Validation and scope
- [ ] Add automated, hardware-independent tests for dataset separation, prompt/format handling, evaluation scoring and error/timeout handling, adapter selection, and comparison calculations, using small fixtures/mocks where appropriate.
- [ ] Run available syntax/unit/dependency/documentation checks before merge and accurately report what passed, failed, or could not run. Do not claim real 4B training or benchmark outcomes unless they were actually measured.
- [ ] Submit a focused Issue-linked PR against `main` and review it according to repository policy. Do not include model binaries, trained artifacts, large dataset copies, or unrelated refactoring.

## Optional validation

- On a sufficiently provisioned Apple Silicon Mac, perform a small end-to-end smoke run (few training steps and a tiny held-out subset), followed by a larger experiment if resources permit; record actual runtime, memory constraints, and results separately. These physical-device runs are useful but are not mandatory when the implementing agent does not have access to suitable hardware.
- Repeat with multiple seeds or an independently authored held-out set to gauge robustness beyond the public benchmark.

## Required post-merge verification

None. No merge-triggered deployment or publication is part of this work.
